correctness.rationale: The projection class computation gives M=(-3,2,-3), with Euler square -2. At beta=-1/2 the imaginary part is 10 n1+5 n0, hence always in 5Z, while Im(M)=5. A finite-slope Jordan-Hoelder decomposition would require two strictly positive imaginary parts summing to 5, impossible. I independently recomputed the HRR scalar, class, Euler pairing and divisibility argument.

equivalent_formulations: At beta=-1/2, the imaginary-part homomorphism on the integral numerical lattice is 5 times an integer and M has minimal positive value 5.

value.rationale: Although short, the lemma removes an entire vertical numerical wall ray for the natural line-projection class and is directly motivated by Bridgeland stability calculations.
